gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much weight you carry per mile of range. A 58-lb BLUETTI Elite 300 gives about 9.5 Model Y miles, or about 6 lb per mile. The 113.5-lb EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 gives about 12.9 miles (8.8 lb per mile), and the 136.7-lb Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus about 12.1 miles (11.3 lb per mile). So the lightest box gets you about three-quarters of the flagship range at half the weight.
standout_why: I compared against the two pages ChatGPT cited. Jackery's FAQ covers only its grounding adapter and 120/240 V ports, with no miles, kWh, time, weight or price. ryzzun.com gives miles by station size (1, 2, 3.84 and 5 kWh at 85% to the car), Level 1 and Level 2 miles per hour, and names the F3800, but it says nothing about weight, price, miles per pound or cost per mile. ChatGPT's own answer only says 2–4 kWh is 'relatively heavy and expensive' and gives no figure. The whichwatts EV guide (result 3) failed to load because of a certificate error, so I could not check it.
decides: For a station you keep in the trunk, weight per mile changes the pick. The BLUETTI Elite 300 (3,014.4 Wh, 57.98 lb) gives about 9.5 miles at 6.1 lb per mile and about $126 per mile at its $1,199 list price. The DELTA Pro 3 and F3800 Plus add only about 3 more miles for 56–79 lb more. Those two still win when time matters: their 240 V output can empty the pack into the car in about 35–45 minutes on Level 2, against about 1 h 47 min for the Elite 300 at Level 1, 12 A. The ALLPOWERS R4000 lists for $1,499 (about $138 per mile), but it is sold out and I could not open a source for its weight.
